title: boost-skills conventions (v1)
description: Slot vocabulary referenced by sandermuller/boost-skills vendor skills. Consumers fill this in their CLAUDE.md Project Conventions block. See https://github.com/sandermuller/boost-skills#project-conventions-schema for the published vocabulary.

schema-version.description: Schema-version discriminator. v1 of the boost-skills conventions vocabulary.

jira.description: Jira issue tracker configuration for jira-create / jira-rework / jira-updates skills.

project_key.description: Single Jira project key for issue creation, updates, and rework lookups (e.g. 'HPB').

refuse_other_projects.description: When true, vendor skills refuse to create or edit (mutate) issues outside of jira.project_key. Cross-project linking and mentions remain allowed.

description_format_doc.description: Path to project-owned doc containing Jira description voice rules, CREATE/UPDATE templates, append-merge algorithm. Validated for file-existence by 'boost doctor --check-conventions'.

github.description: GitHub repository identity. Used by pull-requests, pr-review-feedback, github-issue-updates skills.

owner.description: GitHub owner (user or org) the repo lives under.

default_base_branch.description: Fallback base branch for PR creation when no branch pattern matches. See branches.patterns for per-pattern base resolution.

branches.description: Branch naming patterns + per-pattern base branch resolution. Primary use: vendor pull-requests (and codex-review) skills scan patterns in declared order; first match wins; the matched pattern's base is the PR/review base; no match falls back to github.default_base_branch. Secondary use: the pattern field doubles as a branch-name template for detection — e.g. write-spec matches the current branch against a Jira-keyed pattern to extract {issue_key}.

pattern.description: Branch-name template (e.g. 'feature/HPB-XXXX', 'hotfix/HPB-XXXX-{slug}'). Recognized placeholders are vendor-defined.

base.description: Base branch this pattern's PRs target (e.g. 'develop', 'master').

pr.description: Pull-request creation conventions. Used by the pull-requests skill.

title_format.description: Template for PR titles. Recognized placeholders: {issue_key} (full Jira key like 'HPB-1234'), {short_title}.

template_path.description: Path to the PR template read fresh at PR-creation time. Validated for file-existence by 'boost doctor --check-conventions'. Absent file = vendor skips template injection.

gates.description: Pre-PR gates enforced by the pull-requests skill. v1 vocabulary: skill_invoked, shell_command, mcp_tool. Unknown types are rejected by JSONSchema validation.

type.description: Vendor verifies the named skill was invoked in current conversation before allowing PR creation.

skill.description: Skill name to check for prior invocation (e.g. 'codex-review').

window.description: Time window to check for invocation. 'in_session' = anywhere in current conversation. 'since_last_code_change' = since the most recent Edit/Write tool call to a file NOT in boost-core managed agent paths (.ai/, .claude/, .github/skills/, .agents/, or other paths in the boost-core managed .gitignore block).

on_missing.description: Vendor behavior when gate fails. 'stop_and_request' = halt + ask user to run skill. 'warn' = print warning + proceed. 'skip' = silent skip.

type.description: Vendor runs the shell command and checks exit code before allowing PR creation.

expect_exit_code.description: Expected exit code for gate pass. Non-match fails the gate.

type.description: Vendor invokes the named MCP tool; gate passes when tool returns success. Open escape hatch for project-specific policy not covered by skill_invoked / shell_command.

tool.description: MCP tool name in the tool namespace (e.g. 'qa-approval-check').

args.description: Arguments passed to the MCP tool invocation.

risk.description: Optional PR risk-tier routing for the pull-requests skill. ABSENT ⇒ the skill uses its generic Low/Medium/High risk question (no behavior change). Orthogonal to pr.gates: gates are always enforced; risk tiers are a separate optional layer — a gate-only project never declares risk and is never pushed into a tier. Declaring pr.risk requires at least the tiers array (an empty pr.risk would disable the generic fallback with nothing to route by).

matrix_doc.description: Optional path to a project-owned doc holding the risk-assessment methodology (the subjective how-to-score prose). The tier→routing TABLE is data (see tiers); this doc holds only prose. Validated for file-existence by 'boost doctor --check-conventions'.

assessment_skill.description: Optional host skill the pull-requests skill invokes to score a PR's tier before routing (e.g. 'pr-risk-assessment').

ai_reviewers.description: Default AI reviewers requested across all tiers (e.g. ['copilot', 'codex']). A tier may override via its own ai_reviewers. Hoisted here because it is typically constant across tiers.

tiers.description: Risk tiers in ascending severity. Variable length — no mandated count or names. 'routing' selects the routing model; this version implements 'reviewer_count' only.

label.description: Optional PR label applied for this tier (e.g. 'risk:high').

routing.description: Routing model for this tier. This version implements 'reviewer_count' only. RESERVED future modes (documented, not yet implemented; a later additive minor adds them as enum values): 'codeowners_path' (route by CODEOWNERS path/team ownership), 'blast_radius' (route by semver/public-API impact, for package consumers), 'gate_skill' (route by a gate-skill verdict).

human_reviewers.description: (reviewer_count) Human approvals required for this tier.

require_codeowners.description: (reviewer_count) When true, CODEOWNERS approval is required for this tier.

extra.description: Free-form required-action strings the skill surfaces for this tier (e.g. 'security-tag', 'cab-ticket'). NOT a canonicalized vocabulary — project-defined, surfaced verbatim.

labels.description: Optional mandatory-PR-label policy for the pull-requests skill. ABSENT ⇒ the skill has no label step (no behavior change). Use for a label vocabulary the project must apply to every PR — authorship provenance, change class, compliance tagging — where the choice depends on knowledge only the author has and cannot be derived from the diff. Orthogonal to pr.risk: a risk tier's own 'label' field is routing metadata applied by tier score, this slot is an author-declared policy; a project may declare either, both, or neither. Declaring pr.labels requires at least the options array (a policy with no vocabulary has nothing to apply).

require_exactly_one.description: Exactly one option must be applied. false ⇒ at most one (the label is encouraged, not mandatory).

exempt_bot_authors.description: Skip the policy for PRs authored by a bot (Dependabot, github-actions, autofix bots). Set true when the policy's question cannot be answered for machine-authored PRs. Deliberately says nothing about WHICH bots — bot detection belongs to the tracker query (e.g. GitHub's author.is_bot), not to a name list here that would rot.

rule.description: The single question that decides which option applies, in the project's own words (e.g. 'Who wrote the first working version of the main change?'). Rendered verbatim to the agent and to the author when asked.

rule_doc.description: Optional path to a project-owned doc holding the full policy — rationale, edge cases, exemptions. The option TABLE is data (see options); this doc holds only prose. Validated for file-existence by 'boost doctor --check-conventions'.

options.description: The label vocabulary. Variable length — no mandated count or names — but at least one option, since a policy with nothing to apply is meaningless. The skill re-checks this: a config rejected here still renders.

name.description: The label name exactly as it exists in the tracker. Applied verbatim — never translated, re-cased, abbreviated or re-worded, because these names are typically aggregated outside the repo.

when.description: One-line criterion for choosing this option.

on_doubt.description: This option is the fallback when the AUTHOR is uncertain. At most one option may set it. Not enforced here — expressing 'at most one, zero allowed' needs minContains, which the validator does not honor — so the skill treats a config with several as invalid and asks rather than picking.

testing.description: Testing framework conventions. Used by bug-fixing, test-writing, backend-quality skills.

backend_framework.description: Backend test runner the project uses. Vendor skills invoke the matching runner and follow its conventions.

forbid.description: Test frameworks or category aliases vendor skills must NOT suggest. Atomic framework values: 'dusk', 'panther', 'pest', 'phpunit', 'vitest', 'jest', 'mocha', 'cypress', 'playwright'. Category aliases (expand to atomic sets at vendor runtime): 'js-test-frameworks' = [vitest, jest, mocha, cypress, playwright]; 'browser-test-frameworks' = [cypress, playwright]; 'php-browser-tests' = [dusk, panther]. Adding a new alias is a minor schema bump; removing or redefining an alias is a major bump.

quality.description: Optional automated code-quality tooling conventions. Used by backend-quality and pull-requests skills. ABSENT ⇒ no Rector step (no behavior change).

rector.description: When true, backend-quality Tier 2 (at completion) and the pull-requests preflight run `vendor/bin/rector process` to completion BEFORE Pint, then always run Pint afterward (Rector output is not style-clean). Absent/false ⇒ no Rector step (no behavior change). Opt in explicitly here — skills do NOT auto-detect Rector from a `rector.php` config or a `vendor/bin/rector` binary, so adopting this catalog never changes an existing project's flow until it declares `quality.rector: true`.

codex.description: Codex invocation configuration. Used by codex-review skill.

invocation_mode.description: DEPRECATED and ignored since boost-skills 2.17.0. The codex-review skill now always runs the bounded native-CLI wrapper (`scripts/run-codex-review.mjs`, shipped as a skill companion asset); the plugin-broker path and its `bare_cli` fallback were removed because the broker hung on stale sessions. This key no longer affects behavior — remove it from your conventions. Retained in the schema only so existing configs keep validating.

setup_doc.description: Optional path to a project-owned doc with project-specific codex overrides only (custom auth flow, project-specific focus areas, exclusions). The universal wrapper invocation playbook is folded into the codex-review skill body — most consumers leave this slot unset. Validated for file-existence by `boost doctor --check-conventions` when declared.

spec.description: Spec-file conventions. Used by write-spec, implement-spec, interview skills.

filename_pattern.description: Template for spec filenames. Default when unset: 'specs/{slug}.md'. Recognized placeholders: {issue_key} = full Jira key (e.g. 'HPB-1234'); {slug} = URL-safe kebab-case from issue title or feature name (lowercase, alphanumerics + dashes, no consecutive or leading/trailing dashes, recommended cap ~60 chars truncated on word boundary); {date} = ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Empty-placeholder rule: if a placeholder resolves empty (e.g. {issue_key} when no Jira issue), the placeholder AND any single adjacent dash are omitted. Example: 'specs/{issue_key}-{slug}.md' with no issue + 'Set up dark mode' → 'specs/set-up-dark-mode.md' (not 'specs/-set-up-dark-mode.md').

research_docs.description: Paths to project-owned reference docs vendor skills consult during research phase (architecture docs, relationship maps, glossaries). Each path validated for file-existence by 'boost doctor --check-conventions'.

mcp.description: Project-specific MCP server-name mappings. Each value is the tool-namespace segment as it appears between the 'mcp__' prefix and the '__<tool>' suffix in the actual MCP tool name — NOT the package's npm/composer name. Example: tool 'mcp__laravel-boost__database-schema' → slot value 'laravel-boost'; tool 'mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue' → slot value 'mcp-atlassian'. Vendor skills then resolve 'mcp.<slot>' to call the tool: e.g. with `mcp.jira: mcp-atlassian`, vendor invokes `mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue` at runtime. NOTE: unlike sibling groups, mcp.* INTENTIONALLY allows arbitrary property names — the vocabulary of service keys (jira, laravel, atlassian, github, etc.) is consumer-defined; closing this to a fixed set would force the schema to enumerate every MCP namespace boost-skills knows about, which doesn't match how MCP works in practice.

review.description: Optional PR review-feedback conventions, consumed by the pr-review-feedback skill. ABSENT ⇒ built-in defaults: the built-in bot-reviewer set and the colleague gate ON (a human colleague's threads are never auto-acted on).

bot_reviewers.description: ADDITIONAL author logins treated as automated reviewers (bots), eligible for auto-handling (apply/skip, reply, resolve). EXTENDS the built-in set — it does NOT replace it. The built-in set is always active: the literal logins 'copilot-pull-request-reviewer', 'github-actions', 'codex', plus any login ending in the literal four-character suffix '[bot]' (e.g. 'dependabot[bot]'). Declare here only the extra logins specific to the project (e.g. an org CI bot, a different AI reviewer). A thread is classified 'bot' only when EVERY comment in it is from a bot login; one human comment makes the whole thread 'colleague'.

colleague_gate.description: When true (default, and when this slot is absent), threads containing any human-colleague comment are NEVER auto-acted on — the skill evaluates, presents a recommendation, and lets the user decide whether to apply, reply, or resolve. When false, the skill may auto-handle colleague threads the same way it handles bot threads (full automation) — opt in only when the team accepts the agent acting on human review comments without a confirmation step. Bot-thread auto-handling is unaffected either way.

fixtures.description: Optional test-fixture / code-sample anonymization gate, consumed by the evaluate skill (and inherited by final-verification-review, which runs the full evaluate loop). Guards a package that ships publicly against leaking proprietary product domain — real entity/class names, table/column names, route keys, domain jargon, copied comments — through code samples and fixtures. ABSENT ⇒ evaluate performs no anonymization check (no behavior change).

anonymization.description: Anonymization-gate knobs. Mirrors the translations slot's split: machine-readable knobs here, judgment-criteria prose in the host guideline (which is composed into always-on context). Declaring this object requires at least `guideline`.

guideline.description: Path to the project-owned guideline holding the anonymization policy prose: what counts as proprietary, how to anonymize, placeholder naming conventions. The slot carries only knobs; the judgment criteria live in this always-on doc. Validated for file-existence by 'boost doctor --check-conventions'.

scope.description: Paths the gate scans. Default covers BOTH 'src/' — which SHIPS in the Composer dist archive, making code-sample heredocs there the worst leak surface — and 'tests/', which is typically export-ignored from the archive but still lives in version control. Do not narrow to 'tests/' only.

forbidden_terms.description: OPTIONAL fast-path denylist of literal terms (real product entity names, domain jargon) that must never appear in scoped files — enables a deterministic grep-based check. Absent ⇒ the gate falls back to the judgment criteria in the `guideline` doc.

translations.description: Optional DB-DRIVEN translation-key validation, consumed by the evaluate skill. SCOPED TO DB-DRIVEN KEYS ONLY — keys stored in a database that bypass the framework's file-based translation validation and can be malformed. File-based-only projects (standard Laravel lang files) should NOT declare this; their keys are framework-validated already. ABSENT ⇒ evaluate performs no translation-key check (no behavior change).

key_pattern.description: Per-consumer regex a valid DB-driven translation key must match (NOT a shared constant — each project defines its own, e.g. '^(enum_[A-Za-z0-9_]+|[a-z0-9_]+(\.[a-z0-9_]+)+)$'). evaluate flags DB-driven keys that fail this pattern.

file_based_prefixes.description: Marks keys that are file-based (framework-validated) and therefore EXEMPT from the DB-driven check.

framework_groups.description: Top-level framework lang groups whose keys are file-based and exempt. Baseline covers standard Laravel groups; consumer-extensible.

vendor_namespace_exempt.description: When true, any key matching a vendor namespace prefix (regex '^[\w-]+::', e.g. 'filament::') is file-based and exempt — covers all package-namespaced keys without per-package enumeration.

rules_doc.description: Optional path to a project-owned doc with subjective naming-quality rules (prose). The subjective judgement stays prose; only key_pattern format is enforced as data. Validated for file-existence by 'boost doctor --check-conventions'.
